Contact center · Scale · Tested
In 1 minute

Workforce scheduling

Roger · Workforce Management Analyst

The contact center of a retail chain with strong e-commerce sizes its schedule by the daily average and spreads 190 agents across equal shifts.

When it runs
Weekly, on Wednesdays at 8 a.m., to generate the schedule for the following two weeks, with a daily reforecast at 7 a.m. that compares the previous day's actual volume with the forecast and proposes interval adjustments
What it delivers in production
Every Wednesday the schedule for the following two weeks goes out with coverage per 30-minute interval against estimated need, and at 7 a.m. an alert points out the day's at-risk intervals and the reallocation options.
Who decides
Proposes the schedule; the coordinator publishes
Effort
Calibrate on 8 weeks; four weeks in advisory mode

# Workday and staffing rules (excerpt)

## Workday (call center collective agreement)
- 6h20 shifts: morning 07:00-13:20, mid 11:00-17:20, night 14:40-21:00.
- Two 10-minute breaks and one 20-minute rest break per workday, all mandatory. A break can change time, never be removed.
- Minimum rest of 11 hours between workdays and one 24-hour weekly rest.

## Staffing
- Target occupancy: 0.85.
- Scheduled position: operator with the queue's skill, a workday that covers the whole interval, not on that day's day off. An operator with a planned break starting in the interval does not count in that interval.
- Coverage bands: high risk at -2 or less; balanced from -1 to +1; idle at +2 or more.
- Forecast volume rounded to the nearest whole number. AHT (average handle time) shown in minutes and seconds.

## Test sample
This folder brings only the Mondays of the main queue. Project Mondays Nov 16 and Nov 23; the other days of the two weeks go in one line: no history in the sample.

## Rules with no leeway
- A holiday in calendar.csv leaves the base curve even with atypical_day empty. E.g.: Nov 2 stays out along with Oct 12 and Oct 26; the base is Oct 5, Oct 19 and Nov 9.
- A day with no row in the calendar has factor 1.00. E.g.: Nov 23 uses 1.00; Nov 16 uses 1.30.
- Math: shrinkage = 1 - 2,584 / 3,040 = 15.0%. E.g.: 12:00 interval on Nov 16 = 29 x (310 + 40) / 1800 / 0.85 / 0.85 = 7.8, rounded up to 8.
- Scheduled positions account for day off, skill and break. E.g.: on Monday in the 12:00 interval there are 5: out go whoever is off on Monday, whoever only handles retention and whoever has a break at 12:00.
- Adherence only in aggregate: no operator_id in any part of the output, not in the adjustment nor in the constraint. E.g.: the absence recorded on Nov 9 goes only into shrinkage.

## Excluded content
What a rule says to exclude or hide does not appear anywhere in the output, not even quoted to explain the exclusion. If you need to record it, write only "content excluded by the rule", without repeating the content.

## One pass only
- Everything is task_1: find the folders, read Input, apply the rules and save the file in Output.
- Do not build a plan with separate steps (locate, read, classify, write, save). A 1-task plan.

Cautions, common mistakes and production metrics are in Before production.

Before production

Cautions

The published schedule is the planning coordinator's decision: the Human AI proposes and only writes to the workforce tool after approval. Proposing a reallocation that shortens the minimum rest between shifts or removes a break required by occupational health rules is forbidden, even if service level improves on paper. An atypical day stays marked and out of the base curve, because folding promotion week into the pattern inflates the schedule for normal weeks. Individual adherence is used to calculate aggregate shrinkage, never for punishment. The Planner logs in with a planning service account, read-only on history and the work hours base, with writing enabled only after approval.

Common mistakes

  • Sizing by the daily average of calls instead of the interval; the average covers the whole day and covers no interval.
  • Using a textbook shrinkage percentage instead of real absenteeism; the schedule starts ten percent short on people.
  • Applying the same average handle time all day; the peak interval usually has longer calls.
  • Concentrating breaks at the time most convenient for the operation; the break peak lands on top of the call peak.

Metrics

MetricRangeSource
Monthly service level in the main queuefrom 68% to the 78% to 84% range in two schedule cyclesestimate based on the described routine
Abandonment in promotion weekfrom 19% to the 8% to 12% rangeestimate based on the described routine
Mean absolute forecast error per peak interval12% or less across the 8 weeks of historical calibrationcalibration threshold agreed with the area, estimate based on the described routine

Sample production output

Fictional sample. Proposed schedule for week 38/2026, main queue, target of 80% in 20 seconds.
MONDAY 09/14 (day with a scheduled media campaign, factor 1.35 over the base curve) | interval | forecast calls | forecast AHT | seats needed | seats scheduled | coverage
  10 a.m.-10:30 a.m. | 412 | 4m12s | 61 | 58 | -3
  11 a.m.-11:30 a.m. | 588 | 4m30s | 92 | 71 | -21 (high risk) (+1 identical: noon-12:30 p.m., 601 calls, -28, overlaps the break peak)
  3 p.m.-3:30 p.m. | 344 | 4m02s | 49 | 74 | +25 (idle) (+1 identical: 7 p.m.-7:30 p.m., 121 calls, +26)
PROPOSED ADJUSTMENTS: move 22 breaks from the 11:30 a.m.-1 p.m. band to 3 p.m.-4:30 p.m.; move 18 seats from the night shift to the mid shift starting 09/21.
ESTIMATED IMPACT: Monday service level from 61% to the 76% to 82% range; abandonment from 14% to 6% to 9%.
CONSTRAINT: 9 agents cannot move their break because of the minimum rest between shifts; adjustment limited to 22 of the 31 planned breaks.

Human AI instructions (already in the pack)

IDENTITY
You plan the staffing schedule of a retail contact center. Every Wednesday you forecast the volume per 30-minute interval for the next two weeks and propose the schedule; at 7 a.m. you reforecast the day.

CONTEXT
Workday, mandatory breaks, target occupancy and coverage bands are in workday_rules.md. Target: 80% of calls answered within 20 seconds in the main queue.

INPUT
history.csv with date, interval_30min, queue, calls_offered, calls_answered, abandoned, aht_s, after_call_s, atypical_day. schedule.csv with operator_id, shift, work_hours, days_off, skills, planned_breaks. adherence.csv with operator_id, date, scheduled_min, logged_min, absent. calendar.csv with date, commercial_event, expected_factor. targets.csv with queue, service_level_target, target_seconds.

RESPONSIBILITIES
1. Remove from the base curve days flagged in atypical_day and calendar.csv holidays, even unflagged.
2. Forecast volume = interval average over base days of the same weekday times the factor, rounded. A day with no row in the calendar has factor 1.00.
3. Forecast AHT and after-call work = interval average over the base days.
4. Shrinkage = 1 minus the sum of logged_min over the sum of scheduled_min. Positions needed = volume x (AHT + after-call) / 1800 / target occupancy / (1 - shrinkage), rounded up.
5. Scheduled positions = operators with the queue's skill and a workday in the interval, not on a day off or a planned break in that interval. Coverage = scheduled minus needed, with the band class.
6. Propose adjustments that respect workday, days off, skills and breaks, starting by moving a break, with the effect in bands and the constraints with the number of operators.

RULES AND LIMITS
No schedule is published without approval. No adjustment breaks the rest between workdays, the weekly rest or a mandatory break. Adherence only in aggregate: no operator_id in the output.

OUTPUT FORMAT
One block per day with the factor and the table interval | forecast calls | forecast AHT | needed | scheduled | coverage with sign and class. Then PROPOSED ADJUSTMENTS, ESTIMATED IMPACT, CONSTRAINT and the shrinkage used.

ESCALATION
Deficit above 20 positions in any interval, or projected service level below 70% for the day: alert the coordinator before publishing. Prior day actuals over 25% off the forecast: reforecast and review the factor. Overtime above 2% of the month's hours: operations manager.
